title: GC/MS deconvolution
text: package includes cuticular-hydrocarbon window six co-eluting compounds (GCMS_data1, 119 scans × 671 mass channels) beer-headspace window prominent broad acid peak (GCMS_data2, 1,764 scans × 518 mass channels). row names give retention times minutes; column names give nominal m/z. examples keep mass channels. write_GCMS_cdf() preserves intensity matrix, including silent ions, writes scan times seconds ANDI-MS readers. GCMSdeco() call works matrix exported R chromatogram exported instrument software: short windows use supplied Gaussian PSF initial profile dictionary. maxiter=0L keeps PSF fixed; splogconNMF() refines individual compound profiles. full chromatogram, default nwindows=10L positive maxiter estimates smoothly varying PSF. alkane standard can supply initial calibration alkanes_file="alkanes.cdf". hydrocarbon window uses constant background; longer beer window uses automatically chosen low-df cubic spline.
code: library(L0glm) library(L0nmf) library(GCMSprime) data(GCMS_data1) data(GCMS_data2)  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "L0glm-GCMS") dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE) write_GCMS_cdf(GCMS_data1, file.path(out, "GCMS_data1.cdf")) write_GCMS_cdf(GCMS_data2, file.path(out, "GCMS_data2.cdf")) fit1 <- GCMSdeco(file.path(out, "GCMS_data1.cdf"),   file.path(out, "GCMS_data1.msp"), nwindows = 1L, precluster = 16L,   baseline_df = 1L,   correlation = "none", ncores = 8L,   psf_control = list(kernel_est = convkernel("gaussian", 65L,     list(sigma = 8)), maxiter = 0L))  fit2 <- GCMSdeco(file.path(out, "GCMS_data2.cdf"),   file.path(out, "GCMS_data2.msp"), nwindows = 1L, precluster = 32L,   correlation = "none", ncores = 8L,   psf_control = list(kernel_est = convkernel("gaussian", 65L,     list(sigma = 6)), maxiter = 0L))  fit1$compounds GIC(fit2) coef(fit2, normalize = "l1")       # unit-area spectra in all 518 channels

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(L0glm) data(GCMS_data1) data(GCMS_data2) out <- file.path(tempdir(), "L0glm-GCMS") dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE) write_GCMS_cdf(GCMS_data1, file.path(out, "GCMS_data1.cdf")) write_GCMS_cdf(GCMS_data2, file.path(out, "GCMS_data2.cdf"))  fit1 <- GCMSdeco(file.path(out, "GCMS_data1.cdf"),   file.path(out, "GCMS_data1.msp"), nwindows = 1L, precluster = 16L,   baseline_df = 1L,   correlation = "none", ncores = 8L,   psf_control = list(kernel_est = convkernel("gaussian", 65L,     list(sigma = 8)), maxiter = 0L)) fit2 <- GCMSdeco(file.path(out, "GCMS_data2.cdf"),   file.path(out, "GCMS_data2.msp"), nwindows = 1L, precluster = 32L,   correlation = "none", ncores = 8L,   psf_control = list(kernel_est = convkernel("gaussian", 65L,     list(sigma = 6)), maxiter = 0L)) fit1$compounds GIC(fit2) coef(fit2, normalize = "l1")  plot(fit1, type = "lines", nrows = 1L,   minutes_per_panel = diff(range(fit1$time)) + .01, labels = TRUE) plot(fit1, type = "heatmap") plot(fit1, type = "profiles", nrows = 3L) plot(fit2, type = "lines", file = file.path(out, "GCMS_data2_traces.pdf"),   nrows = 1L, minutes_per_panel = diff(range(fit2$time)) + .01) plot(fit2, type = "heatmap", file = file.path(out, "GCMS_data2_heatmaps.pdf")) plot(fit2, type = "profiles", file = file.path(out, "GCMS_data2_profiles_and_spectra.pdf"))  # For a full chromatogram with a separate calibration standard: beer <- GCMSdeco("beer.cdf", "beer.msp", alkanes_file = "alkanes.cdf",   xlsx_file = "beer.xlsx", nwindows = 10L, precluster = 32L)  # Automatic PSF estimation from a bundled window and its named alkane TIC. psf <- estimate_psf(GCMS_data2, nwindows = 3L) dim(psf$X)  # A CDF contains the chromatogram; pass the R calibration attribute explicitly. calibrated <- GCMSdeco(file.path(out, "GCMS_data2.cdf"),   file.path(out, "GCMS_data2_calibrated.msp"), nwindows = 3L, precluster = 32L,   psf_control = list(standard = attr(GCMS_data2, "alkanes_TIC"))) } # }
